title: Compute tight-binding band structures
action: Implement the 4×4 tight-binding Hamiltonian for a helical atomic chain using Löwdin orbitals s, p_η, p_τ, p_z with first and second nearest neighbor interactions, as described in the paper’s Theory section. Use the overlap parameters from Table 1 (first and second nearest neighbor V_ssσ, V_spσ, V_ppσ, V_ppπ) and orbital energies E_s = -17.239 eV, E_p = -6.857 eV. Use interatomic distance d = 2.9 Å. For each of the three geometries: linear (R=0, θ=0), helix with pitch 125 Å (R=3.25 Å, θ=0.1439 rad), and helix with pitch 50 Å (R=3.25 Å, θ=0.3375 rad), construct the Hamiltonian matrix for at least 200 uniformly spaced k in [-0.5, 0.5], diagonalize to obtain the four eigenvalues, and output the band energies. Scale second-neighbor overlap parameters appropriately based on the interatomic distances for each geometry.
description: Electronic band energies E(k) for all four bands and three geometries. The checker will recompute the Hamiltonian and compare the submitted energies within a tight tolerance to verify correct implementation.
output_schema: CSV file with columns: k (float, the k-point value), band (int, 0-3 indexing the four bands), E (float, band energy in eV), geometry (string: 'linear', 'helix125', 'helix50'). Must contain at least 200 k-points per geometry and all four bands.
